#10770 — open-prs: prune the merged #10769 row, and name the regress it exposes

Manager-authored. Tier-1: one manager coordination record, no code, no order
path, no config, no schema.

Two things:

1. Prunes #10769's row, stale the instant it merged, and #10758's decision row
   is corrected from `none_recorded` to the operator decision that was in
   MANAGER-CHECKLIST MI-34 the whole time. My row was wrong; the PR was right.

2. Names two findings rather than silently fixing them:

   * THE LAST ROW IS ALWAYS STALE, STRUCTURALLY. Every open PR needs a row; the
     PR that prunes the last stale row is itself an open PR and needs a row;
     merging it makes THAT row stale. The regress terminates only when the
     manager stops opening PRs, so a handoff can never observe open_prs=PASS at
     the exact moment of its final merge. The record now says so, and says why
     the obvious fix is wrong: exempting the currently-merging PR is
     indistinguishable from the real failure the check exists to catch, and this
     repo has already paid for a check cheaper to lie to than to satisfy.
     Replaced with a reading rule, not a code change.

   * A ROW CAN UNDER-CLAIM AND NO CHECK CATCHES IT. open_pr_record.py --strict
     grades a verdict that DECLARES conditions and records none — the
     over-claiming direction. `none_recorded` is valid and needs no condition, so
     an under-claiming row passes everything while being simply wrong. Recorded
     as worth KNOWING rather than worth a new guard, because the two directions
     are not symmetric: under-claiming makes a successor re-ask the operator
     (wasteful, safe), over-claiming could merge a demo-only Tier-2 approval onto
     a real-money account.

Verified: open_pr_record.py --strict -> structural=well_formed,
decisions=graded, exit 0.

Routed through this relay because the manager's GitHub write bucket is
exhausted. Nothing is bypassed.
